items.q: In the management of PIGN/IRGN, serum C3 is low in what proportion of patients?
items.exp: Investigations in PIGN/IRGN: serum C3 is low in 60% of patients (in contrast to 90% in PSGN). (Book p777)

items.q: The biopsy findings described for PIGN/IRGN are:
opts: IgA-predominant ± C3 deposits, or C3-predominant deposits with a garland/rope pattern
Linear IgG along the GBM with crescents
C3-dominant deposits with camel-hump subepithelial humps
No immune deposits, with pauci-immune crescentic GN
items.exp: PIGN/IRGN biopsy: IgA-predominant ± C3, or C3-predominant deposits showing a garland/rope pattern. (Book p777)

items.q: A 5-year-old with post-streptococcal GN has C3 measured at presentation, and his cousin with MRSA-related infection-associated GN is also tested. The expected results are:
opts: ↓C3 in 90% of PSGN versus ↓C3 in 60% of PIGN/IRGN (the p775 table printing ↑C3 in 60% for PIGN)
↓C3 in 60% of PSGN versus ↓C3 in 90% of PIGN/IRGN
Normal C3 in both conditions, since C3 falls only in RPGN
↑C3 in 90% of PSGN versus ↓C3 in 60% of PIGN/IRGN
items.exp: PSGN shows a low C3 in 90% of patients; for PIGN/IRGN the text states a low C3 in 60% of patients, while the p775 table prints '↑C3 (in 60%)' — learn both printings and note the discrepancy. (Book p777)

items.q: A renal biopsy from a patient with staphylococcal infection-related GN shows C3-dominant deposits arranged in an arc around the glomerular capillary wall. This appearance is called:
opts: Garland/rope pattern
Camel-hump pattern
Starry sky pattern
Tram-track pattern
items.exp: PIGN/IRGN biopsy shows IgA-predominant ± C3 or C3-predominant deposits in a garland/rope pattern. (Book p777)

items.q: The prognosis and management described for PIGN/IRGN are:
opts: Poor prognosis — management includes vancomycin (nephrotoxic) and dialysis
Good prognosis — antibiotics alone cure the renal lesion
Poor prognosis — high-dose steroids are the mainstay
Good prognosis — no treatment is required at all
items.exp: Treatment section: poor prognosis; vancomycin (nephrotoxic) and dialysis are listed. (Book p777)

items.q: Steroids are the mainstay of treatment for PIGN/IRGN, while antibiotics reliably reverse the RPGN.
opts: False — steroids worsen cellulitis and other antibiotics do not treat RPGN
True — steroids are indicated in every case
True, but only if serum C3 is low
False — vancomycin is nephroprotective here
items.exp: The note states that steroids worsen cellulitis and that other antibiotics do not treat the RPGN of PIGN/IRGN — hence the poor prognosis. (Book p777)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT listed in the treatment of PIGN/IRGN?
opts: High-dose corticosteroids
Vancomycin (nephrotoxic)
Dialysis
Antibiotic therapy of the staphylococcal infection
items.exp: Treatment listed for PIGN/IRGN is vancomycin (nephrotoxic) plus dialysis; steroids are specifically warned against because they worsen cellulitis. (Book p777)

items.q: Fill up: In PIGN/IRGN the antibiotic named in treatment is ______, which is nephrotoxic.
opts: vancomycin
amoxicillin
erythromycin
cefazolin
items.exp: Treatment of PIGN/IRGN includes vancomycin, noted to be nephrotoxic, along with dialysis for the renal failure. (Book p777)
